headline: Red Sox keep rolling with shutout win at Camden Yards
morning_brew: Sonny Gray was absolute dynamite on the mound, carving through the Orioles for seven innings and giving us exactly the kind of performance this rotation has been hunting for. A five-run cushion in a hostile environment like Camden Yards is a luxury I don't get to enjoy often, and seeing the bullpen close it out without any drama was a welcome change of pace. We're holding that second wild card spot firm, and with nineteen games left on the schedule, every single one of these wins is a beautiful deposit in the Duck Boat fund.

The bats were swinging with purpose, piling up nine hits to keep the pressure on Baltimore all night long. It wasn't about one hero, but just a steady, professional effort from the lineup that kept the scoreboard ticking in our favor. Seeing the team string together a solid, mistake-free game after the intensity of the last few days tells me these guys are finally locked in on what we need to get to October. My mother watched the final out and just nodded, saying it was the most comfortable she has felt watching a game in weeks, and I know exactly what she means.

We have another one at Baltimore this afternoon, and I am not looking past that to see what is coming next week. Neighbor Rick is currently in day four of his umpire dossier, scouring the rulebook for some conspiracy theory about the strike zone, but honestly, I am just enjoying the fact that we are playing winning baseball. This team has carved out a rhythm, and if we can just keep our heads down and keep grinding, we will be exactly where we need to be when the leaves start turning.
